tips.text: Hit with Precision Protocol, then wait a moment before the second attack. The delayed recast hits much harder and turns part of its damage into true damage.
Aim Tactical Sweep so the enemy is in the outer half of the cone. That part slows them, deals extra damage and heals you.
Fire Hookshot at a wall, then recast to dash at the enemy champion. You travel twice as far toward champions, and the enemy is stunned on arrival.
Use Hookshot to dodge enemy skillshots, or to escape. You can dash away from the wall without an enemy nearby.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum to trap your lane opponent in a zone they can't leave. Fight them inside it, because your attacks deal bonus magic damage to them.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum to interrupt a channel. It also knocks other enemies away from the fight.
Trade by hitting the enemy when your shield from Adaptive Defenses is ready. It blocks one damage type, so you win the trade.
Cast Tactical Sweep during the wind-up of Precision Protocol's attack. Doing so does not cancel the attack, so you can pack more damage into a short trade.

combos.name: Wall hop
combos.when: When you want to cross a thin wall or reposition quickly, especially in the jungle or around the river.
combos.text: Hookshot to the wall, then recast Hookshot in your chosen direction. Camille crosses thin walls and the dash range extends toward enemy champions.

combos.name: Flash Hookshot recast
combos.when: When you need to change the angle of your Hookshot dash or surprise a target.
combos.text: While attached to the wall, Flash and recast Hookshot within a brief window to dash from the new spot. It's hard for enemies to predict.

tips.text: Land Tactical Sweep so the outer half of the cone hits the enemy; they get slowed, take extra damage, and you heal.
Use Hookshot on a wall near the enemy, then recast to dash into a champion and stun them for your team to follow up.
Wait a moment before the second Precision Protocol attack; a delayed recast hits much harder and deals some true damage.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum on the enemy carry; it traps them in a zone and knocks other enemies away from you.
Pick off isolated targets with Hookshot while the enemy team is busy fighting your team.

combos.name: Wall hook, flash, dive
combos.when: You are perched on a wall and want to dive an enemy who is standing out of normal Wall Dive range.
combos.text: While you hang on the wall, Flash toward the target and recast within a moment. The recast dashes from the Flash spot and the stun still lands.

tips.text: Dodge The Darkin Blade by stepping sideways or dashing with Hookshot; its hit zones are telegraphed and the first one is a narrow line.
Hit Aatrox with the outer half of Tactical Sweep. He is slowed, and you heal and deal extra damage based on his max health.
Step toward Aatrox or out to the side of Infernal Chains to leave its pull area. Walking straight away is much harder.
Use Precision Protocol twice in a trade, waiting a moment before the second hit for true damage. Stun with Hookshot to land both.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum to trap Aatrox when he is low or has used his dash. His World Ender revive can't be used while he is trapped away from you.
Use Hookshot to dash onto Briar when she walks up; if you hit her you stun her, which cancels her chance to trade freely.
Hit Briar with the outer edge of Tactical Sweep. It slows her, deals extra damage and heals you.
Save The Hextech Ultimatum for when Briar commits in a fight. It locks her in a zone she cannot leave, even with dashes.
Delay your second Precision Protocol attack a moment so it hits much harder and deals true damage through her healing.
Dodge Apprehend by moving out of its cone, or hook away with Hookshot. Without it, Darius has few ways to pull you in.
Hit Darius with the outer edge of Tactical Sweep. It slows him and heals you.
Poke with Precision Protocol while Apprehend is on cooldown, and do not stand in melee for long once his Hemorrhage stacks build.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum to trap Darius in a fight you can win; he cannot escape the zone, but keep your health high against his burst.
Do not dive in with Hookshot while Fiora has Riposte ready. She can turn your stun back on you.
Wait out Riposte before you cast The Hextech Ultimatum on Fiora. Its brief parry can negate your lock-in.
Hit Fiora with the outer half of Tactical Sweep to slow her and heal yourself. Her Lunge closes gaps fast, so aim it where she will land.
Watch the Vital marked on you. Fiora will try to strike from that side, so move so she cannot line it up.
Don't stand next to a Powder Keg; Gangplank can detonate it for heavy damage and a slow. Walk out of the blast area.
Hit a keg yourself to defuse it when it is the safe option; an enemy destroying a keg only dismantles it.
Wait until Gangplank uses Remove Scurvy before you go for Hookshot and The Hextech Ultimatum, or the stun is wasted.
Hit Gangplank with the outer half of Tactical Sweep to slow him and heal yourself when he tries to set up kegs.
Once Gangplank is level 6, stay away from low health and don't run in a straight line; Cannon Barrage can hit you from anywhere on the map.
Hit Garen with the outer edge of Tactical Sweep to slow him and heal, but he can clear it with Decisive Strike.
Keep your distance from Garen when Decisive Strike is ready; his hit silences you and stops your abilities.
Step out of Judgment's range instead of trading inside it; it deals big damage when you are the only one near him.
Use Hookshot to stun Garen and land both Precision Protocol hits while he is stunned.
Do not use The Hextech Ultimatum on Garen when he is nearly dead; he cannot flee, but his Demacian Justice finishes you if you are low.
Poke Garen from range and keep hitting him; any damage stops his Perseverance healing.
Dive onto Jayce with Hookshot, then recast to stun him when he is in hammer range. Close the gap quickly, because he wins at range.
Hit the outer half of Tactical Sweep on Jayce. It slows him and heals you.
Save The Hextech Ultimatum for when Jayce has used Thundering Blow. It traps him so he can't kite you with range.
Dodge Shock Blast by walking sideways. It stops at the first enemy it hits, so it can't pass through minions.
Don't waste Hookshot to dash at K'Sante early; his Ntofo Strikes can slow you and then stun and pull you in once it has two stacks.
Hit K'Sante with the outer half of Tactical Sweep. He is slowed and you heal, and his large health makes the bonus damage count.
Trade in short bursts. Delay your second Precision Protocol attack so it deals bonus damage, then step back.
Be careful when K'Sante goes All Out. He becomes much squishier, so that is your window to fight him.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum to trap K'Sante when his Path Maker is on cooldown. Without it, he has little to break out of your zone and fight.
Don't walk into Malphite's Ground Slam range for a long trade; it cuts your Attack Speed and your damage.
Use Tactical Sweep on Malphite's outer edge to slow him and heal, but expect his armor to blunt the damage.
Land both Precision Protocol hits; wait before the second so it deals more damage and part becomes true damage, which ignores his armor.
Stay out of Malphite's Seismic Shard range when his Unstoppable Force is ready; his knock up can start a bad trade.
Use Hookshot to stun Malphite and start your trade, then break his Granite Shield before you commit.
Keep Tactical Sweep's outer edge on Mordekaiser; it slows him and heals you.
Stay out of Death's Grasp's line; it pulls you into his Darkness Rise aura.
Trade in short bursts and back off once his Darkness Rise aura is on; staying close costs you health.
Hit him with Hookshot's stun when he commits, then leave before his Indestructible shield grows.
Save your movement spells for Realm of Death; you're cut off from your team inside it.
Hit Rumble with the outer edge of Tactical Sweep; it slows him and heals you.
Go in when Rumble Overheats; he cannot cast spells, so Hookshot onto him and stun him for a free trade.
Do not stand in The Equalizer's fire. Walk out of it quickly or you take heavy damage.
Dodge Electro Harpoon where you can; getting hit twice makes you much slower and easier to burn down.
Rumble deals magic damage, so your Adaptive Defenses shield will often block magic when you hit him.
Stay out of Sion's line when he is charging Decimating Smash. If he holds it long, step aside or dash out before he releases it.
Hit the outer edge of Tactical Sweep to slow Sion and heal off him. Use it to close in or to leave.
Wait for Sion to use Soul Furnace before you commit. The shield soaks your damage, and he can detonate it on you if you stay close.
The Hextech Ultimatum traps Sion and adds damage to your attacks. Back off once he dies, because Glory in Death brings him back as a zombie.
Use Hookshot to dodge Roar of the Slayer or to reach Sion. A stun from Hookshot's dash can set up your Precision Protocol hits.
Dash in with Hookshot to stun Teemo, then attack him up close. He is weak when you are on top of him.
Walk through brush carefully. Teemo can hide there and ambush you with Toxic Shot.
Use the outer part of Tactical Sweep on Teemo to slow him and heal. It wins you trades once he is close.
Watch for Noxious Trap before you dash in. Stepping on one slows you and shows where you are.
Save The Hextech Ultimatum for when Teemo cannot run away with Move Quick. It locks him in a zone.
Hit Vayne with Hookshot's follow-up dash to stun her. Once she is stunned, land your attacks on her.
Do not stand against a wall when Vayne has Condemn ready. A knockback into terrain stuns you and deals heavy damage.
Aim Tactical Sweep so Vayne is in the outer half. She is slowed, you heal, and you can close the gap.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum on Vayne at level 6. She cannot escape the zone, and Tumble will not carry her out of it.
Vayne is fragile, so push the pressure on her early. Wait for her to use Tumble, then go in.
Use Tactical Sweep so the outer half of the cone hits Yone; he is slowed and you heal, which wins a short trade.
Land Hookshot on Yone, then stun him and swing both Precision Protocol attacks while he cannot answer.
Wait a moment before the second Precision Protocol attack; the delayed hit deals much more damage and part of it is true damage.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum on Yone when he is low or committed; he cannot escape the zone, and Soul Unbound back to his body ends it.
Hit Yone with your basic attacks to trigger Adaptive Defenses; he deals mixed damage, so the shield may block only part of it.
Stay out of a straight line with Bard. If Cosmic Binding hits you and then a wall or another enemy, you get stunned.
Walk over Bard's shrines to destroy them, and do it before his ally can pick them up.
Hit Bard with the outer half of Tactical Sweep. He is slowed and you heal from the extra damage.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum on Bard or his carry to trap them for a fight. It also interrupts channels.
Wait out Tempered Fate before you dive. Anything inside it cannot be hurt for a short time.
You can follow Bard through his Magical Journey portal, but only if the other side is safe.

comboRefs.note: Hookshot flash dive reaches Bard even when he stands out of range, such as after using his portal.

tips.text: Hug the side of lane and walk around Inner Flame; it stops at the first unit it hits, so stay behind minions.
Break Focused Resolve's tether by moving out of range, or you will be rooted.
Dive with Hookshot when Inspire is on cooldown. Karma's shield absorbs your burst.
Hit Karma with the outer edge of Tactical Sweep. She is squishy, so you slow her and heal.
Leave the fire circle quickly after Karma's empowered Inner Flame lands; it slows and then bursts for heavy damage.
Stay out of Zenith Blade range. If it hits, Leona dashes in and roots you, and a stun follows.
Do not fight into Eclipse when it is up. Wait for her shield to detonate, then trade.
Use Tactical Sweep with its outer edge on Leona to slow her and heal yourself.
Once you are close, Hookshot into an enemy champion to stun nearby enemies. Do it when Leona's Shield of Daybreak is on cooldown.
At level 6, step out of the center of Solar Flare quickly; only the center stuns.
Hookshot off a wall at Lulu to stun her, but expect Whimsy; she can turn you into a critter mid-dash.
Dodge Glitterlance by stepping out of line; it slows you and makes Tactical Sweep hard to land.
Save The Hextech Ultimatum for Lulu or her carry once Whimsy is used; it locks them in with you.
Hit the enemy carry on the outer edge of Tactical Sweep to slow them and heal back poke damage.
Stay out of Lux's Light Binding line, and keep a minion between you when you hook in, as it hits only the first two enemies.
Hit Lux with Hookshot's dash when her Light Binding is on cooldown; she has little to stop you and the stun lets you kill her.
Hit Lux with the outer edge of Tactical Sweep to slow her and heal yourself.
Walk around Lucent Singularity instead of through it, and leave before it blows up.
At level 6, use The Hextech Ultimatum on Lux; she cannot escape and her Final Spark is hard to line up.
Look for Milio when he has no ally close by; alone he is easy to reach, so Hookshot onto a wall and Recast to stun him.
Hit him with the outer half of Tactical Sweep. He is slowed and you heal back some health.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum on Milio or his carry to trap them. Your attacks then deal extra damage to that target.
Keep your distance from Ultra Mega Fire Kick; it can stop your dive. Walk out of its line, and do not dash in a straight line toward him.
Walk up and use Hookshot to reach Nami, then Recast to stun her. Nami's bubble is her best answer, so only go in when it is on cooldown.
Once Nami misses Aqua Prison, move in and trade, because she has no stun again for a long while.
Hit with the outer part of Tactical Sweep to slow Nami and heal yourself. Use it when she steps forward to heal or poke.
Hold your fight while the enemy carry has Tidecaller's Blessing on them. It fades quickly, so wait it out and then trade.
Land both Precision Protocol attacks by waiting before the recast. The delayed hit deals much more damage, some of it true damage.
Step out of the path of Tidal Wave when you see it coming. It travels slowly.
Stay out of Nautilus's Dredge Line lane. Keep a minion between you and him, because the anchor stops on the first enemy it hits.
Hookshot away from a Dredge Line, but note that her hookshot can't be cast while grounded or rooted. Use it before he has the chance to root you.
Hit the outer half of Tactical Sweep on Nautilus; it slows him and heals you.
Wait out the Riptide waves before you run, or you walk into the later explosions.
Don't trade into Nautilus while his Titan's Wrath shield is up; wait for it to break or expire.
Step to the side of Pantheon when he braces with Aegis Assault. He is only immune from the front, so don't fight into the shield.
Keep your health up. Pantheon's thrown Comet Spear hurts more against low-health targets and can finish you.
Use Hookshot to dash onto Pantheon after he commits his jump. The stun gives you time to trade.
Hit Pantheon with the outer half of Tactical Sweep. It slows him and heals you.
Move away when Grand Starfall starts. It warns you before he lands.
Stay away from Pyke when he has been hidden; he heals back damage you dealt once you lose sight of him, so finish the trade while he is visible.
Hit Pyke with the outer half of Tactical Sweep; he is slowed and you heal from the extra damage.
Keep Hookshot ready as an escape. Pyke's pull and stun are dangerous if you are caught out, so dash away before he commits.
Stay behind your minions when Pyke charges Bone Skewer; the harpoon ends at the first unit it hits.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum on Pyke or his lane partner to lock them in a zone where they cannot flee, then win the fight inside it.
Wait until Senna has used Last Embrace before you dive in with Hookshot; once it is gone, she has little way to stop you.
Hit Senna with the outer half of Tactical Sweep so she is slowed and you heal.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum on Senna when you can reach her. She cannot walk or dash out of the zone, and her allies are knocked away.
Use the stun from Hookshot's recast, then land both Precision Protocol attacks while she is stunned. Her range is long, so you have to close the gap.
Stay out of Seraphine's line; Beat Drop slows you, and a slow already on you turns it into a root.
Seraphine has no escape, so look for Hookshot onto a wall and then a dash to stun her.
Hit Seraphine with the outer half of Tactical Sweep; it slows her and heals you.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum on Seraphine when she is out of position; she cannot escape the zone.
Dive Sona with Hookshot when she is exposed. Her Crescendo stun is her best answer, so wait until you are ready.
Sona is fragile and has little to stop you once you reach her. Aim Tactical Sweep so the outer edge hits her, slowing her and healing you.
Sona's Hymn of Valor hits the nearest two enemies, so stay back from her poke. Step up only when you can go in.
Her empowered attack from Song of Celerity slows you, so close on her when she lacks a ready empowered hit.

comboRefs.note: The Flash-extended Hookshot dive reaches Sona, a champion who has no listed dash to escape it.

tips.text: Stay out of Death Sentence's line, especially next to minions. Sidestep once you see Thresh begin the throw, because the cast is slow.
Use Tactical Sweep so the outer half of the cone hits Thresh. It slows him and heals you.
Hit Thresh with Hookshot's dash recast to stun him. Follow with Precision Protocol while he can't move.
Use The Hextech Ultimatum on the enemy carry. It knocks Thresh away and keeps him out of the fight.
The Hextech Ultimatum has a short range, so Thresh's Flay can push you off before you land. Cast it once Flay is on cooldown.

comboRefs.note: The Flash-extended Hookshot stun can reach a Thresh standing outside normal Wall Dive range.
